director.chapterArc: Monumental arrival and exhausted hope narrow into Nell’s ledger arithmetic. Toren converts the threat of separation into cold resolve, mistakes inheritance for currency, then makes the more dangerous offer of Rook’s life. Rook’s quiet refusal forces Toren to state the group’s true bond; that moral victory settles into provisional solidarity. The closing training sequence replaces negotiation with methodical fear-conditioning and ends on an unresolved commitment north.
director.restraintNote: Keep Toren’s desperation physically contained: calculation first, streaming eyes only when the words finally expose his grief. Nell remains a ledger even when compassion briefly enters. Rook’s boundary is most frightening at low volume. After the negotiation, drain the emotion promptly; training is clinical, spatially exact, and only dryly funny.

cues.delivery: Let Nell’s brief pity register as an unwanted human interruption, then discipline it back into exact trade knowledge; the refusal to exploit him is practical, not tenderly consoling.
cues.from: Then she looked up at him, and her face changed, and what came into it was the thing Toren had not been braced for, because he had braced for greed and for haggling and for being laughed at.
cues.through: "That's what I'm asking." She did not touch it. "It's yours. That's the whole of what's wrong with it. Put it in my hand, and it's a grey stone. Put it in his hand" — she tipped her chin at Rook — "and it's a grey stone. There's a man in Coldwater buys them off estates, and he pays what the metal's worth, and the metal's worth about two weeks of grain, and he does it because every so often a child turns thirteen and takes to one that's been sitting in a drawer, and he can sell it on to a family for a year's work. That's the trade. That's the entire trade." She pushed it back across the book towards him with two fingers. "I'd be taking a dead thing off a boy who doesn't know it's dead. I've done worse. Not that."
cues.reason: Nell recognizes that Toren is offering a dead inheritance and chooses not to profit from his ignorance.

cues.delivery: Hold the shock almost flat, as Toren reconstructs what he witnessed in his father’s hands; weight the failure of understanding, never invite tears.
cues.from: Toren stood with his hand on it.
cues.through: Toren picked the Ember up and closed his fist on it, and it was cool, and the door at the bottom of his head was still open, and he was still standing in a weigh-yard where the arithmetic came out the same as it had a minute ago.
cues.reason: The artifact’s worthlessness becomes a belated recognition of his father’s condition and sacrifice.

cues.delivery: Toren argues like a frightened protector who has forced himself into competence: build through evidence and terms, keeping the voice steady and the appeal free of pleading.
cues.from: "Two days ago in the Coldwater cut, we got hit by husks. Forty of them. Fifty. Nobody counted, there wasn't time. There were eight of us, and we lost three, and we'd have lost all eight, and then that man came down the rock face and shut the road." He put his hand flat on the table. "He shut the road, ma'am. Wall to rail. He put his hand down on the road bed, and nothing came through it, and he held it there with thirty of them stacked against it while we got a cart up the road. I watched him do it, and so did all three of them, and you can ask them separately if you think I'm lying."
cues.through: "You've got a north face that loses people," Toren said. "So don't buy an Ember. Buy him. A season on the north face. And in exchange my grandmother gets a bed in the sick-house, a real one, when one comes free before anybody else's name, and all four of us stay unbonded and together and go up on the spring convoy."
cues.reason: He turns desperation into a strategically persuasive offer meant to keep the group and Senna alive.

cues.delivery: Allow Nell’s ledger voice to soften only enough to reveal the lives behind the arithmetic; make the offer grave, specific, and immediately contain the compassion.
cues.from: "A season," said Nell, quietly, all the ledger gone out of her voice for the first time. "Rook. I've got eleven names on the north face this year. I'd give you the girl's placement and the little one's and the shed and the bed and I'd give you the convoy, and I'd do the paperwork wrong in six places and let the board find out afterward. For a season. You know what that's worth. You've seen the face."
cues.through: "A season," said Nell, quietly, all the ledger gone out of her voice for the first time. "Rook. I've got eleven names on the north face this year. I'd give you the girl's placement and the little one's and the shed and the bed and I'd give you the convoy, and I'd do the paperwork wrong in six places and let the board find out afterward. For a season. You know what that's worth. You've seen the face."
cues.reason: Nell briefly abandons pure transaction and exposes what Rook’s service could save.

cues.delivery: Place Toren’s fear beneath Rook’s absolute quiet. Rook does not flare or threaten; each clause calmly establishes the boundary Toren crossed and the unseen cost he tried to price.
cues.from: He said it to her, and then he turned around and said it to Toren, and his voice had gone somewhere Toren had not heard it go before.
cues.through: "You put a season of my life on a table in front of a woman with a book. That's what you just did. Whatever else you thought you were doing, that's what happened." He was not shouting. It would have been easier if he had been. "I told all four of you at the cut. Two days. To the wall. In front of the people here. I have been late to something for a long time, and you don't know what it is, and you had no right to price it."
cues.reason: Rook’s refusal is the chapter’s emotional climax, frightening because it is controlled rather than shouted.

cues.delivery: Begin with stripped-down certainty, then let the accumulated losses press against an otherwise unshaking voice. The streaming eyes and the argument must remain separate: the body breaks, the logic does not.
cues.from: "Because I'd have done it anyway," Toren said.
cues.through: "You can go. Nobody's stopping you, and nobody's owed you. But you don't get to hand us to somebody with a book and call that the same thing as putting us somewhere." He swallowed. "And I'm not signing. And they're not staying if I'm not, and you can ask them, and you'll find out I'm right, and I don't much like that I know that."
cues.reason: Toren finally names his father’s sacrifice and refuses to let the survivors be divided.

cues.delivery: Give Nell’s validation without sentimentality: she is correcting the shame he will carry tonight, then returning him to the harder lesson about knowing the value of an offer.
cues.from: "That was well done," she said, "and I want you to hear from somebody with no stake in it that it was well done, because you're going to spend tonight thinking you made a fool of yourself with a stone." She let go. "You'll make a lot of offers in your life. Learn what you're holding before you put it on a table."
cues.through: "That was well done," she said, "and I want you to hear from somebody with no stake in it that it was well done, because you're going to spend tonight thinking you made a fool of yourself with a stone." She let go. "You'll make a lot of offers in your life. Learn what you're holding before you put it on a table."
cues.reason: Nell grants Toren a brief, earned kindness while preserving her transactional authority.

cues.delivery: Treat the absurd shouting and Milo’s cracked laughter as involuntary pressure release, dry and slightly ragged rather than playful.
cues.from: He made all four of them shout. That was the strangest part of the whole hour. Not words at first, just noise, over and over, until Milo was hoarse and laughing at the same time in a slightly unhinged way.
cues.through: He made all four of them shout. That was the strangest part of the whole hour. Not words at first, just noise, over and over, until Milo was hoarse and laughing at the same time in a slightly unhinged way.
cues.reason: This is the chapter’s first genuine release after the negotiation, though exhaustion keeps it unstable.

cues.delivery: Deliver the forecast clinically, as a timetable rather than a scare story; make the three-second window precise and useful, with no action-film bravado.
cues.from: "Because in about a week something is going to come at you from the side, and you will see it three seconds before anyone else does, and you will not say anything, because you'll be busy being frightened, and those three seconds are the only useful thing you'll have." He looked down the line at them. "So you're going to learn to make a noise on purpose while you're frightened. That's tonight. That's all of tonight."

He looked down the line at them. "So you're going to learn to make a noise on purpose while you're frightened. That's tonight. That's all of tonight."
cues.reason: Rook explains that the drill is conditioning for a predictable failure under fear.

cues.delivery: Keep the geography and assigned roles exact. Let fear accumulate in an orderly way without accelerating past the mechanics; Milo’s repeated calls are strained but precise, and the kill is barely competent, not triumphant.
cues.from: And then, because the light was going and because there was drift-smell on the wind off the river, he took them a quarter mile downstream to where two husks were nosing at a dead thing in the shallows, and put the four of them in a line on the bank with the water at their backs, and said, "Right. There's two. Nothing behind you but the river, so nothing gets behind you. Toren in the middle, Wyck on the left because you're strong and you're slow, Dessa on the right, Milo behind Dessa's shoulder and your only job is to say where the second one is, out loud, every second, until it's down."
cues.through: They killed both of them. Barely. Wyck took a raking cut across the forearm that bled a lot and mattered little, and Toren's spike went out twice and came back twice, and Milo called the second husk's position eleven times in a voice like a cracked bell and got it right every single time.
cues.reason: The controlled exercise becomes real violence while testing whether the group can act and communicate under pressure.

cues.delivery: Use bone-dry instructional obstruction: Rook’s logic is maddeningly coherent, and his agreement with Dessa should land without a smile or any loosening of authority.
cues.from: "Two of them you'll find on your own in about three days," said Rook, "and you'll learn them properly that way. Two of them I'll tell you when they're about to kill you, which is the only time anybody actually listens. And two of them I'm not telling you yet."
cues.reason: The exchange releases tension through Rook’s severe, deadpan teaching method.
